library_rail.decade.description: The Library rail's band for a decade of release years (2020s) when the list is sorted by Release date. {decade} arrives as the decade's first year in plain digits (2020, 1990) and the string says "the decade that starts there" the way the language writes it shortest. Keep it short: it stands in a narrow column beside the posters, about 100 px at the rail's 22 px type, so a longer native phrase ("Années 2020", "Anni 2020", "2020-as évek") may not fit.

library_rail.hours.description: The Library rail's band for a length in whole or half hours (3h, 2½h, 1h) when the list is sorted by Duration. {hours} arrives formatted for the language and already carries the half (2½); the unit and its spacing are the language's own short hour, the same as core.duration_hours writes it. Keep it short: it stands in a narrow column beside the posters.

library_rail.hours_or_more.description: The Library rail's top Duration band (3h+): at least this many hours. {hours} arrives formatted; the unit is the language's own short hour, as in library_rail.hours, and the + follows it. Keep it short.

library_rail.today.description: The Library rail's first band when the list is sorted by Date added, Date viewed or Last episode added: items from today. The same word as under_posters.value_today, unless that is too wide for the rail's narrow column beside the posters (about 100 px at the rail's 22 px type): then its usual abbreviation. One short word.
